events.title: Thuban - The Ancient North Star
events.fact: Thuban (Alpha Draconis) was the North Star for ancient Egyptians. The Great Pyramid's descending passage was aligned with it.

events.title: Great Pyramid Construction
events.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built during this era, aligned with the stars that were different from today due to precession.

events.title: Stonehenge Era
events.fact: Stonehenge was in active use. The stars visible from there have shifted positions noticeably since then.

events.title: Egyptian Star Catalogs
events.fact: Ancient Egyptians created some of the first known star catalogs. Many constellation patterns were similar to today.

events.title: Greek Astronomy Flourishes
events.fact: Greek astronomers like Hipparchus began systematic star observations. They wouldn't recognize some stars' current positions!

events.title: Turn of the Common Era
events.fact: The 'Star of Bethlehem' was recorded around this time. Stellar positions were slightly different from today.

events.title: Ptolemy's Almagest
events.fact: Ptolemy compiled the most detailed ancient star catalog with 1,022 stars. Our fast movers have shifted since then!

events.title: Medieval Arab Astronomy
events.fact: Islamic astronomers refined star positions. Many star names we use today (like Betelgeuse) come from Arabic.

events.title: Galileo's Telescope
events.fact: Galileo first turned a telescope to the night sky, revealing countless stars invisible to the naked eye.

events.title: First Stellar Parallax
events.fact: Friedrich Bessel measured the first stellar distance, proving stars were incredibly far away.

events.title: Barnard's Star Measured
events.fact: E.E. Barnard discovered the fastest-moving star in our sky - moving 10.3 arcseconds per year!

events.title: Gaia DR3 Reference Epoch
events.fact: ESA's Gaia spacecraft measured positions of 1.8 billion stars with unprecedented precision. This is our reference year!

events.title: Present Day
events.fact: You are viewing the current sky. Some stars have moved measurably even since Gaia's measurements!

events.title: Future Sky - Vega Era
events.fact: Around 13,700 AD, Vega will become the North Star. The night sky will look noticeably different.

events.title: Distant Future
events.fact: Fast-moving stars like Barnard's Star will have shifted by degrees - visible changes to the naked eye!

events.title: Constellation Dissolution
events.fact: Many familiar constellations will be unrecognizable. Orion's Belt stars are moving in different directions!
